name: Adobe Photoshop
tagline: Industry-standard raster image editor with layers, masking, retouching and generative AI fill.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Photoshop is not a feature, it is thirty-five years of accumulated image math, color management, file format handling and pixel-level tooling that half the visual world has muscle memory for. An agent can absolutely one-shot a browser canvas editor with layers, blend modes, masks and a few filters, and that will genuinely cover cropping, resizing and light retouching. What it will not produce is CMYK and ICC profile correctness, 16-bit-per-channel and raw pipelines, PSD read and write fidelity, content-aware fill, or generative fill that anyone would ship. The AI features specifically are not code, they are trained models plus the licensing arrangements that make their output commercially usable. Free alternatives already exist and are far more complete than anything you will build in a session, which is the honest signal here.
coreLoopDIY: A local browser image editor: open a file, stack layers with blend modes and opacity, paint raster masks, apply crop, transform, curves and blur, then export PNG or JPEG.
requirements: A modern browser with WebGL2 or WebGPU
No accounts, everything runs locally in the browser
whatYouLose: Generative fill, content-aware fill and every other trained-model feature, plus the commercial usage rights that come with Adobe's versions
Color management: ICC profiles, CMYK, soft proofing, print-ready output
PSD interchange with anyone else, including clients and printers who will demand it
Raw processing, 16 and 32 bit pipelines, smart objects, adjustment layer stacks, non-destructive filters
Twenty years of tutorials, keyboard shortcuts and hiring assumptions built on the real thing
moatNotes: The PSD file format is its own moat: it is the handoff currency between designers, agencies and printers, and it is barely documented.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because Photoshop is the interchange layer for professional image work, not just an app. A client sends a PSD, a printer asks for CMYK at a specific profile, a job posting lists it as a requirement, and a retoucher's hands already know every shortcut. The generative features tightened that grip: they are trained models with indemnified output, which is a thing you cannot reproduce with a weekend of code no matter how good the agent is. Hobbyists genuinely should use the free alternatives; everyone whose invoice depends on file compatibility keeps paying.
notes: A layer stack is a weekend; a color-managed pixel pipeline and a trained inpainting model are not. The moat is PSD as the industry's handoff format plus generative models with licensed, indemnified output.
prompt:
Build a local, offline raster image editor that runs entirely in the browser. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry, no cloud calls.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind for UI
- Canvas 2D for compositing (skip WebGL, correctness over speed)
- Zustand for editor state
- No server. Files are read and written via the File System Access API with a hidden input fallback.

In scope:
- Open PNG, JPEG, WebP. Multiple images become multiple layers.
- Layer panel: reorder by drag, rename, toggle visibility, opacity slider, blend mode (normal, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, difference), delete, duplicate.
- Per-layer raster mask: brush and eraser with adjustable size and hardness, painting white or black into the mask. Mask thumbnail in the panel.
- Transform per layer: move, scale from handles, rotate, flip horizontal and vertical.
- Adjustments applied per layer, non-destructive, stored as parameters and recomputed on render: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue shift, levels with black/white/gamma, and a curves widget with a draggable spline on the RGB composite.
- Filters, destructive, applied on confirm: gaussian blur, unsharp mask, add noise, grayscale.
- Crop tool with aspect ratio presets (free, 1:1, 4:5, 16:9) that resizes the document.
- Canvas: zoom with ctrl+wheel, pan with space+drag, fit-to-window button, checkerboard for transparency.
- History: undo/redo stack, at least 50 steps, cmd+Z and shift+cmd+Z.
- Export flattened PNG or JPEG with a quality slider. Also save/load the whole project as a single .json plus embedded base64 layer bitmaps in one file.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- PSD read or write, CMYK, ICC profiles, raw files, 16-bit channels
- Any generative or AI feature, any inpainting, any model download
- Text layers, vector paths, smart objects, plugins

Requirements:
- Keep the render pipeline in one well-commented module: layers bottom to top, apply adjustments, apply mask, composite with blend mode.
- Render at document resolution offscreen, then draw scaled to the viewport. Do not lose pixels on zoom.
- Debounce re-renders so a slider drag stays responsive at 4000x3000.
- README with setup, keyboard shortcuts, and a blunt paragraph on what this cannot do compared to Photoshop.
